record.original_question: For a finite group G, let χ1(G) denote the totality of the degrees of all irreducible complex characters of G with allowance for their multiplicities. Suppose that H is a finite group with χ1(H) = χ1(G). If G has trivial solvable radical, must H also have trivial solvable radical?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite group, and let Irr(G) denote the set of irreducible complex characters of G. Define χ₁(G) to be the multiset of character degrees
  χ₁(G) = {{ χ(1) : χ ∈ Irr(G) }},
that is, the collection of degrees of all irreducible complex characters of G counted with multiplicities. The solvable radical of a finite group is its (unique) largest normal solvable subgroup.

Suppose H is a finite group with χ₁(H) = χ₁(G) (equality of multisets). Assume that G has trivial solvable radical. Must H also have trivial solvable radical?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as a recently posed question in the latest update of the Kourovka Notebook collection of open problems in group theory. Related problems on whether finite groups are determined by the multiset of character degrees have only been resolved for special families (e.g., alternating groups, sporadic simple groups, the Tits group), and no general resolution of this specific question about preservation of trivial solvable radical was found.

status_evidence.title: Alternating and Sporadic Simple Groups are Determined by Their Character Degrees
status_evidence.snippet: If G is a finite group with cd*(G) ⊆ cd*(H) then G ≅ H, for G an alternating, sporadic simple group, or Tits group.
status_evidence.claim: Related determination questions for the multiset of character degrees are resolved only in special cases, indicating the general question remains open.
